title: Mouse Without Borders fails to pair: "Could not load or update pairing" (Negotiation → Connecting → Error)

judgment.rationale: The original two-PC report documents extensive network controls; newer replies confirm persistence on 0.102.3001.0. One user says removing the remote MWB service and rebooting restored operation, while another cannot generate or accept a key. The same release has a confirmed SettingsSync signer rejection tracked in #50795, but this issue has not supplied that exact error or service-state evidence; do not assume either cause or propose a competing fix.
evidence: The original two-PC 0.102.2933 report describes a 24-second failure and Negotiation → Connecting → Error after private-network/firewall/key/IP/admin/VPN/restart controls were tried.

Four later comments confirm generic failure on 0.102.3001.0; one reports recovery after removing the remote MWB service and rebooting, while another still cannot generate/accept a key after two reboots.

#50795 independently documents `Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature` and mismatched trusted signer certificates on 0.102.3001.0. Current source uses exact trusted leaf-certificate equality, but #51567 has no such error excerpt, so this is a possible shared cause, not an established duplicate: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/Utilities/NamedPipePeerVerification.cs#L265-L334
No attachment is present; the latest commenter says key generation and receipt still fail on 0.102.3001.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Correlate one failed key/pairing attempt with its exact SettingsSync error and service mode before routing to #50795 or a separate investigation

fix_assessment.rationale: If the first error is the confirmed signer rejection, route coverage to #50795; otherwise use the observed service/key state to identify a distinct branch. Do not propose a second fix for the same signature mismatch.

proposed_fixes.title: Attribute the first local key/SettingsSync failure before a separate MWB fix
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis only: the generic error may mask the release signer rejection already confirmed in #50795, or a separate local service/key synchronization failure; comments do not identify which error occurs first.
plan: Capture the exact Settings-side error and MWB service/user mode from one failed key-generation or pairing attempt on an affected machine.
If the report contains the #50795 `untrusted-signature` rejection, keep the fix under #50795; otherwise investigate only the service/key branch demonstrated by the report.
Do not repeat the network controls already recorded or change credential handling without evidence of the first failure.
verification: The affected machine generates/synchronizes a key in its reported service mode, and pairing completes or reports the distinct first local/network failure instead of masking it as a generic error.

confidence.rationale: Persistence and a relevant release-level failure are evidenced, but this issue lacks the exact Settings error and service-state correlation.

issue_context.summary: Multiple users report MWB pairing or key synchronization failure on 0.102; one recovery followed remote-service removal and reboot, while other reports remain unresolved.
known_information: The original reporter used matching 0.102.2933 builds on two PCs and already tried private-network/firewall/key/IP/admin/VPN/restart controls without success.

Four comments confirm generic failure on 0.102.3001.0; one reports recovery after removing the remote MWB service and rebooting, and a later comment says key generation/acceptance still fail after two reboots.
#50795 confirms `untrusted-signature` on 0.102.3001.0 with the same valid Microsoft signer pair assigned to opposite Settings/MWB executables; #51567 itself does not include that exception.
inferences: The #50795 signer mismatch could explain some key/SettingsSync failures in this release, but is not established for every #51567 reporter without the local exception text.
Service-removal recovery could indicate stale service state or a reboot-related recovery; that comment does not isolate which action fixed the machine.
issue_context.analysis: The issue already answers common network-control questions; do not repeat them. The diagnostic fork is the first SettingsSync error and service state when key generation/receipt fails. The #50795 rejection is a possible common path; service removal may indicate a separate one. Request the established bug report from a still-affected endpoint rather than assume a duplicate.
initial_investigation: Refreshed the complete body and all five comments; no attachment is present. Comments include three generic 0.102.3001 confirmations, one service-removal/reboot recovery, and a report that key generation/receipt still fail.

Inspected the current peer policy at upstream main 9227a8497750 and compared it with #50795's exact error/certificates; relevant mechanism is not shown by #51567: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/Utilities/NamedPipePeerVerification.cs#L265-L334
Preserved the already-tried network/firewall/key/IP/admin/VPN/restart controls; no generic network checklist is requested.

information_gaps.information: The first SettingsSync error and MWB service/user mode when key generation/receipt fails on an affected 0.102.3001.0 endpoint.
information_gaps.why_needed: The `untrusted-signature` rejection would place the report under #50795; a different first error or service state supports a distinct local key/service investigation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On a machine that still fails, attempt New key or one pairing attempt, note its time and whether MWB runs as user or service, then comment /bugreport immediately. If two PCs are involved, attach both endpoint reports; do not post the security key or repeat the network controls already tested.

actions.label: Capture the first MWB key-sync failure

comment.body: Thanks for the extensive network checks and newer-version confirmations. The service-removal/reboot recovery is useful, but another report still cannot generate or accept a key. A separate #50795 report confirms the exact `untrusted-signature` SettingsSync rejection on 0.102.3001.0; it would explain this only if that exception is present on the affected machine. On a machine that still fails, could you try New key or one pairing attempt, note the time and whether MWB is running as user or service, then comment /bugreport immediately? If two PCs are involved, please attach both reports. Do not post the security key; there is no need to repeat the firewall or network tests already listed.
